Map simulated event/censoring times onto an assessment-time interval

Source: R/interval_censoring.R
add_interval_censoring.Rd

Adds interval-censoring bounds to an already-simulated (and, if applicable, already right-censored – see "Ordering" below) events data frame: given a visit schedule, an event known to have occurred exactly at sim_time is only detectable at the first visit at or after it, and a censored subject is only known event-free through their last visit at or before their own censoring time. Works on the output of sim_tte_ode, sim_tte, or sim_tte_df alike, same as add_censoring.

Usage

add_interval_censoring(
  events,
  visits,
  id_var = "ID",
  time_var = "sim_time",
  status_var = "sim_status"
)

Arguments

events

Data frame of simulated outcomes: typically the $events element returned by sim_tte_ode, or the output of sim_tte/sim_tte_df, optionally after add_censoring. Needs ID, sim_time, sim_status columns by default (rename via id_var/time_var/status_var). Every other column is left untouched, and so are these three: this function only adds sim_time_left/sim_time_right (see "Return" below).

visits

A visit schedule, either:

a numeric vector

applied to every subject (e.g. c(0, 4, 8, 12, 24)). Must start at 0 and be strictly increasing (sorted, no duplicate visit times).

a data frame

with ID/time columns, for a per-subject schedule. Every ID in events must have a schedule (starting at 0, strictly increasing), and every ID in visits must be one that appears in events.

visit_schedule builds the data-frame form from a fixed spacing plus optional per-subject jitter, rather than this function accepting a jitter spec itself – see its own documentation.

id_var, time_var, status_var

Character scalars naming the subject-ID, event/censoring-time, and status columns of events. Default "ID"/"sim_time"/"sim_status".

Value

events with two new columns:

sim_time_left

Left (open) bound of the interval, L.

sim_time_right

Right (closed) bound, R, or Inf for an interval with no known upper bound (a censored subject, or an event that occurred after the subject's last visit and so was never confirmed by the schedule – sim_status still reads 1 in that case: the exact columns are the simulation's ground truth, unaffected by this mapping. The two columns answer different questions: sim_status says what happened, the bounds say what the schedule could observe).

An event with sim_time_left == 0 (an event before the first post-baseline visit) is a left-censored observation – the event is known to have occurred before sim_time_right, exact time unknown – with no separate mechanism needed; see the vignette's "Left censoring" subsection for a worked example. sim_time/sim_status/sim_reason (if present) are returned unchanged – this function only adds columns, so every existing consumer of those three keeps working. For survival::Surv(time = sim_time_left, time2 = sim_time_right, type = "interval2"), which expects NA rather than Inf for an open upper bound, convert with ifelse(is.infinite( sim_time_right), NA, sim_time_right) – see the vignette's "Interval censoring" section for a full worked example.

Ordering with right censoring

Call this after add_censoring (or after the exact simulation, if no independent right censoring was requested), not before: the interval mapping reads sim_time/sim_status as given, so a dropout applied afterward would leave the already-added interval columns stale and inconsistent with the final exact columns. sim_tte_ode's own censoring/ visits convenience arguments apply them in this order internally.

See also

visit_schedule, to build a per-subject schedule with fixed spacing and optional jitter; thin_visits, to drop visits at random (missed visits, dropout); visit_schedule_informative, for visits that react to the simulated outcome. add_censoring, which should run first. sim_tte_ode, which can apply this step itself through its visits argument.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- sim_tte_ode(model = "exponential", param = list(H0 = 0.05),
  n = 50, end = 24, delta = 2, seed = 1)
#> Loading model from cache.
out <- add_interval_censoring(sim$events, visits = c(0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24))
head(out)
#>   ID  sim_time sim_status     sim_reason sim_time_left sim_time_right
#> 1  1 24.000000          0 administrative            24            Inf
#> 2  2 19.770560          1          event            16             20
#> 3  3 11.142509          1          event             8             12
#> 4  4  1.925641          1          event             0              4
#> 5  5 24.000000          0 administrative            24            Inf
#> 6  6  2.143028          1          event             0              4
# }
